s241.content:
Cornelius was elected pope during a time of persecution. He held that Christians who had denied the faith under torture could be readmitted after penance, against the rigorist priest Novatian, who set himself up as a rival pope.

Supported by St. Cyprian of Carthage, Cornelius upheld the Church’s mercy toward repentant sinners. He died in exile and is honored as a martyr, sharing his feast with Cyprian.
s241.intercession: Pope St. Cornelius, pray for us. Teach the Church to welcome back sinners with mercy, and keep us united in faith. Amen.

s242.content:
Sixtus II was pope for only about a year. During the persecution of the Emperor Valerian, soldiers found him celebrating the liturgy in the catacomb of St. Callixtus and beheaded him in his chair, along with four deacons.

His deacon St. Lawrence was martyred a few days later. Sixtus is named in the Roman Canon of the Mass.
s242.intercession: Pope St. Sixtus, pray for us. Strengthen all who worship God in danger, and help us to love the Mass above all things. Amen.

s243.content:
Hippolytus was a learned priest of Rome and one of the most important theologians of his day. Disagreeing with the popes over how to treat repentant sinners, he allowed himself to be set up as a rival pope.

Both he and Pope St. Pontian were exiled to the mines of Sardinia, where tradition says they were reconciled before their deaths. The Church honors both as martyrs on the same day.
s243.intercession: St. Hippolytus, pray for us. Heal divisions in the Church, and help us to be reconciled with those from whom we are estranged. Amen.

s244.content:
Vincent was the deacon of Bishop Valerius of Saragossa in Spain, who had a speech impediment, so Vincent preached for him. During Diocletian’s persecution both were arrested.

Vincent endured the rack, iron hooks, and a red-hot gridiron with such calm that his jailer was converted. He died in prison. He is one of the most honored martyrs of Spain and a patron of Lisbon.
s244.intercession: St. Vincent, pray for us. Make us bold to speak for the Gospel, and patient in every trial. Amen.

s245.content:
Alban was a pagan living in the Roman town of Verulamium in Britain when he sheltered a Christian priest fleeing persecution. Moved by the priest’s prayer, he became a Christian.

When soldiers came, Alban put on the priest’s cloak and gave himself up in his place. He was beheaded on the hill where St Albans Cathedral now stands, the first recorded Christian martyr of Britain.
s245.intercession: St. Alban, pray for us. Teach us to shelter those in danger and to give ourselves for others, as Christ gave Himself for us. Amen.

s246.content:
Vitus was a boy from Sicily, raised a Christian by his nurse Crescentia and her husband Modestus against his pagan father’s wishes. Tradition says he healed the emperor’s son but would not sacrifice to the gods.

He was martyred with Modestus and Crescentia as a young teenager. In the Middle Ages he was counted among the Fourteen Holy Helpers, and the nervous disorder once called "St. Vitus’ dance" is named for him.
s246.intercession: St. Vitus, pray for us. Protect young people, and bring healing to those with nervous disorders and epilepsy. Amen.

s247.content:
According to legend, Margaret was the daughter of a pagan priest in Antioch who became a Christian and refused to marry a Roman governor. In prison, the devil appeared to her as a dragon and swallowed her, but the cross she held burst it open.

She was beheaded for her faith. One of the Fourteen Holy Helpers and one of the voices heard by St. Joan of Arc, she is invoked by women in childbirth.
s247.intercession: St. Margaret, pray for us. Protect mothers and children in childbirth, and help us overcome every temptation by the power of the Cross. Amen.

s248.content:
Erasmus, also called Elmo, was bishop of Formia in Italy and one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers. Legends tell of many tortures he survived during the persecution of Diocletian.

Sailors took him as their patron, and the blue electrical glow that sometimes appears on ships’ masts during storms became known as "St. Elmo’s fire," taken as a sign of his protection. He is also invoked against abdominal pain.
s248.intercession: St. Erasmus, pray for us. Protect sailors and all who travel by sea, and bring relief to those in pain. Amen.

s249.content:
Anastasia is said to have been a Roman noblewoman who visited and cared for Christians imprisoned during the persecution of Diocletian. She was arrested in Sirmium and burned alive.

She is named in the Roman Canon of the Mass, and in the traditional liturgy the second Mass of Christmas, the Mass at Dawn, includes a commemoration of her. She is invoked by weavers and the persecuted.
s249.intercession: St. Anastasia, pray for us. Bless all who visit prisoners and comfort the persecuted. Amen.

s250.content:
Pachomius was a young Egyptian conscripted into the Roman army, where Christians brought food to him and his fellow soldiers. Moved by their kindness, he was baptized after his release.

After years as a hermit, he founded a monastery at Tabennisi where monks lived together under a common rule rather than alone. By his death his communities held thousands of monks and nuns. He is called the father of community monastic life.
s250.intercession: St. Pachomius, pray for us. Bless all who live in religious communities, and help us to love one another in common life. Amen.

s251.content:
Mary left home at twelve and lived for years in Alexandria as a prostitute. She joined a pilgrimage to Jerusalem out of curiosity, but an invisible force kept her from entering the church of the Holy Sepulchre.

Weeping, she prayed before an icon of Our Lady and was then allowed in. She went into the desert beyond the Jordan and lived there as a penitent for forty-seven years. The monk Zosimas met her just before her death.
s251.intercession: St. Mary of Egypt, pray for us. Help all who are trapped in sin to find their way to God’s mercy, and give us true repentance. Amen.

s252.content:
Damasus was pope during the struggle against Arianism. He commissioned his secretary, St. Jerome, to revise the Latin Bible, work that grew into the Vulgate.

He restored the catacombs and composed verse inscriptions for the tombs of the martyrs, many of which survive. During his reign Christianity was declared the official religion of the Roman Empire.
s252.intercession: Pope St. Damasus, pray for us. Help us to love the Scriptures and to honor the witness of the martyrs. Amen.

s253.content:
Paulinus was a wealthy Roman senator and governor. After the death of their only child, he and his wife Therasia gave away their fortune and moved to Nola near Naples to live a life of prayer and hospitality near the tomb of St. Felix.

He was chosen bishop of Nola and wrote fine Christian poetry and letters to friends such as St. Augustine and St. Jerome. He shares his feast with Sts. John Fisher and Thomas More.
s253.intercession: St. Paulinus, pray for us. Help us to hold our possessions lightly and to use them for the glory of God and the good of others. Amen.

s254.content:
Melania was one of the richest women in the Roman world. After the deaths of their two children, she and her husband Pinian freed thousands of slaves and gave away vast estates across the empire.

They fled to North Africa as the Goths sacked Rome, knew St. Augustine, and finally settled in Jerusalem, where Melania founded monasteries on the Mount of Olives.
s254.intercession: St. Melania, pray for us. Free us from attachment to wealth, and help us to share generously with those in need. Amen.

s255.content:
Clotilde was a Burgundian princess who married Clovis, king of the Franks. Through her patient prayers and example, and after a battle in which he called on her God, Clovis was baptized on Christmas Day around 496, along with thousands of his warriors.

This made France the "eldest daughter of the Church." Widowed and grieved by her sons’ violent quarrels, she spent her last years in prayer at Tours.
s255.intercession: St. Clotilde, pray for us. Bless wives who pray for their husbands, and bring peace to divided families. Amen.

s256.content:
Radegund was a Thuringian princess captured as a child by the Frankish king Clothar I, who later forced her to marry him. After he had her brother murdered, she fled the court and became a nun.

She founded the Abbey of the Holy Cross at Poitiers, which received a relic of the True Cross. For the occasion the poet Venantius Fortunatus composed the hymn "Vexilla Regis," still sung in Holy Week.
s256.intercession: St. Radegund, pray for us. Comfort all who suffer in unhappy marriages, and help us to find our refuge in the Cross. Amen.

s257.content:
Brendan was an Irish abbot who founded monasteries including Clonfert. The famous Voyage of St. Brendan tells how he set out with monks in a leather boat to search for the "Promised Land of the Saints" across the Atlantic.

In 1976–77 an explorer sailed a replica leather boat from Ireland to Newfoundland, showing that such a voyage was possible. He is a patron of sailors and travelers.
s257.intercession: St. Brendan, pray for us. Protect sailors and travelers, and make our whole life a voyage toward the promised land of heaven. Amen.

s258.content:
Aidan was an Irish monk of Iona sent at the request of King Oswald to bring the Gospel to Northumbria. He founded a monastery on the tidal island of Lindisfarne and walked the countryside to speak with everyone he met.

He gave away gifts from kings to the poor and ransomed slaves, some of whom became monks. St. Cuthbert saw a vision of angels carrying his soul to heaven on the night he died.
s258.intercession: St. Aidan, pray for us. Make us gentle messengers of the Gospel to everyone we meet. Amen.

s259.content:
Kevin was an Irish hermit who withdrew to the remote valley of Glendalough in the Wicklow Mountains, where he lived in a cave above a lake. Disciples gathered around him, and the monastery he founded became a great center of learning.

A famous legend says a blackbird laid her eggs in his outstretched hand while he prayed, and he held still until the chicks had hatched.
s259.intercession: St. Kevin, pray for us. Teach us patience and gentleness toward all God’s creatures, and help us to find Him in silence. Amen.

s260.content:
Willibrord was an English monk trained in Ireland who led a band of missionaries to Frisia, in today’s Netherlands. Consecrated archbishop by the pope, he made Utrecht his see.

He founded the abbey of Echternach in Luxembourg, where his shrine draws a famous dancing procession every Whit Tuesday. He is called the "Apostle of the Frisians."
s260.intercession: St. Willibrord, pray for us. Bless the Church in the Netherlands and Luxembourg, and give us zeal to share the faith. Amen.

s261.content:
Walburga was an English nun who went to Germany at the invitation of her relative St. Boniface to help in his missionary work. She became abbess of the double monastery of Heidenheim, ruling communities of men and women.

She was known for healing the sick. Oil that seeps from her tomb in Eichstätt has been collected by pilgrims for over a thousand years.
s261.intercession: St. Walburga, pray for us. Bring healing to the sick, and help us to serve the Church wherever we are sent. Amen.

s262.content:
Hubert was a nobleman who loved hunting. According to legend, while hunting on Good Friday he saw a stag with a crucifix between its antlers and heard a voice calling him to turn to God.

He gave up his worldly life, became a priest, and succeeded his teacher as bishop of Maastricht, later moving his see to Liège. He is the patron of hunters, foresters, and mathematicians.
s262.intercession: St. Hubert, pray for us. Help us to see Christ in the world around us and to turn to Him with all our hearts. Amen.

s263.content:
Edmund was the young Christian king of East Anglia when a great Viking army invaded England. Captured, he refused to share his kingdom with the pagan invaders or to renounce his faith.

He was tied to a tree, shot with arrows, and beheaded. Bury St Edmunds grew up around his shrine, and he was honored as a patron of England for centuries.
s263.intercession: St. Edmund, pray for us. Give leaders the courage to remain faithful to God whatever the cost. Amen.

s264.content:
Dunstan was an English monk, a skilled metalworker, musician, and illuminator. As abbot of Glastonbury and later archbishop of Canterbury, he led a great revival of monastic life in England.

He was a trusted adviser to several kings and helped write the coronation rite still used for English monarchs. Legend says he once seized the devil’s nose with red-hot tongs.
s264.intercession: St. Dunstan, pray for us. Bless all who work with their hands, and renew the life of the Church. Amen.

s265.content:
Ludmila was a Bohemian duchess who was baptized with her husband, Duke Bořivoj, probably by St. Methodius. She raised her grandson, St. Wenceslaus, in the faith.

Her daughter-in-law Drahomíra, jealous of her influence, had her strangled at Tetín castle. She is honored as the first Czech martyr and a patron of grandmothers.
s265.intercession: St. Ludmila, pray for us. Bless grandparents who pass on the faith to their grandchildren. Amen.

s266.content:
Olga ruled the Kievan Rus’ as regent after her husband was murdered, and at first took fierce revenge on his killers. Later she traveled to Constantinople and was baptized there.

She tried to bring Christianity to her people, but her son refused. Her grandson, St. Vladimir, would complete her work. She is honored in both the Catholic and Orthodox Churches.
s266.intercession: St. Olga, pray for us. Help those who govern to turn from vengeance to mercy, and bless the peoples of Ukraine and Russia. Amen.

s267.content:
Adalbert, a Czech nobleman, became bishop of Prague but struggled against the paganism and violence of his flock, twice leaving the city. He became a monk in Rome.

He then set out as a missionary to the pagan Prussians on the Baltic coast, where he was killed. He is a patron of Bohemia, Poland, and Hungary, and his shrine is in Gniezno.
s267.intercession: St. Adalbert, pray for us. Bless missionaries who go where the Gospel is unknown, and give us courage when we fail. Amen.

s268.content:
Vladimir was a violent pagan prince of Kiev who, according to the Russian Primary Chronicle, sent envoys to study the religions of his neighbors. Those who visited the great church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople said they did not know whether they were in heaven or on earth.

Vladimir was baptized around 988 and had his people baptized in the Dnieper River. He became known for his care for the poor.
s268.intercession: St. Vladimir, pray for us. Help us to be transformed by the beauty of God, and bless the peoples of Ukraine and Russia with peace. Amen.

s269.content:
Olaf Haraldsson was a Viking warrior who was baptized in Normandy and returned to Norway to become king. He worked to make his country Christian, building churches and bringing in clergy from England.

Driven into exile, he returned with an army and was killed at the Battle of Stiklestad. Miracles at his tomb in Trondheim made him Norway’s national saint, "Norway’s Eternal King."
s269.intercession: St. Olaf, pray for us. Bless the people of Norway, and help us to give our strength to the service of Christ. Amen.

s270.content:
Henry was Holy Roman Emperor and a devout ruler who supported Church reform, founded the diocese of Bamberg, and built its cathedral.

He and his wife, St. Cunigunde, had no children. He is said to have wished to become a monk, but the abbot of Saint-Vanne ordered him under obedience to continue ruling. He is a patron of Benedictine oblates and of the childless.
s270.intercession: St. Henry, pray for us. Help those in power to rule as servants of God, and comfort couples who long for children. Amen.

s271.content:
Hildebrand was a Benedictine monk who served several popes before being elected himself. He led the "Gregorian Reform" against simony and clerical marriage, and insisted that the Church, not kings, should appoint bishops.

In 1077 Emperor Henry IV stood barefoot in the snow at Canossa for three days to seek his pardon. Later driven from Rome, Gregory died in exile, saying: "I have loved justice and hated iniquity; therefore I die in exile."
s271.intercession: Pope St. Gregory VII, pray for us. Keep the Church free and holy, and give us courage to love justice. Amen.

s272.content:
Hugh was a French Carthusian monk brought to England by King Henry II to lead the first Carthusian house there. As bishop of Lincoln he rebuilt the cathedral, cared for lepers, and defended Jews from mob violence.

He fearlessly stood up to three kings. A wild swan befriended him and followed him about, so he is often pictured with it.
s272.intercession: St. Hugh, pray for us. Give us courage to defend the vulnerable and to speak the truth to the powerful. Amen.

s273.content:
Homobonus, whose name means "good man," was a married cloth merchant of Cremona in Italy. He saw his business as a gift from God, dealt honestly, and gave a large part of his profits to the poor.

He died while attending Mass, during the Gloria. He was canonized just two years later, one of the first laymen canonized who was neither a king nor a martyr. He is a patron of business people.
s273.intercession: St. Homobonus, pray for us. Help business people to work honestly and to use their wealth for the poor. Amen.

s274.content:
Hyacinth was a Polish priest who met St. Dominic in Rome and became one of his first friars. He carried the Dominican order back to Poland and preached across Scandinavia, Prussia, Lithuania, and Ruthenia.

A famous legend says that while fleeing a Tatar raid on Kyiv he carried the Blessed Sacrament and a heavy statue of Mary, which became miraculously light. He is called the "Apostle of the North."
s274.intercession: St. Hyacinth, pray for us. Make us tireless in carrying Christ and His Mother to others. Amen.

s275.content:
Agnes was a Bohemian princess betrothed to the Emperor Frederick II, but she refused all marriages to give herself to Christ. With the support of her brother, the king, she founded a hospital and a monastery of Poor Clares in Prague, where she became abbess.

She corresponded with St. Clare of Assisi. Her canonization in November 1989, days before the Velvet Revolution, was seen by Czechs as a sign of hope.
s275.intercession: St. Agnes of Prague, pray for us. Teach us to prefer Christ to every earthly honor. Amen.

s276.content:
Rose was a girl of Viterbo in Italy who, after a serious illness, began preaching in the streets against the Emperor Frederick II, who was at war with the pope. She and her family were exiled.

She tried to enter a convent of Poor Clares but was refused because she had no dowry. She died at about eighteen. Each year the people of Viterbo honor her by carrying a towering illuminated shrine through the streets.
s276.intercession: St. Rose of Viterbo, pray for us. Help young people to speak boldly for Christ, and comfort those who are turned away. Amen.

s277.content:
Margaret lived for nine years as the mistress of a nobleman and bore him a son. When he was murdered, she was led by his dog to his body, and the shock brought about her conversion.

She made public penance in Cortona, became a Franciscan tertiary, and founded a hospital for the poor. Her mystical experiences of Christ were recorded by her confessor. She is a patron of single mothers and the homeless.
s277.intercession: St. Margaret of Cortona, pray for us. Help single mothers and all who are trying to begin again, and give us true sorrow for our sins. Amen.

s278.content:
Roch was a young Frenchman who gave away his inheritance and set out as a pilgrim to Rome. Finding Italy ravaged by plague, he cared for the sick and healed many with the sign of the cross.

When he caught the plague himself, he withdrew to a forest, where a dog brought him bread each day. He is invoked against plagues and contagious diseases, and is the patron of dogs.
s278.intercession: St. Roch, pray for us. Protect us from contagious disease, and bless all who care for the sick at risk to themselves. Amen.

s279.content:
Elizabeth was a princess of Aragon married at twelve to King Denis of Portugal, an unfaithful husband. She bore his neglect with patience, cared for his illegitimate children, and spent her days in prayer and works of mercy.

She repeatedly made peace between her husband and their rebellious son, once riding between their armies on the battlefield. As a widow she became a Poor Clare tertiary. She is a patron of peace.
s279.intercession: St. Elizabeth of Portugal, peacemaker, pray for us. Bring peace to families and nations torn by conflict. Amen.

s280.content:
John was vicar general of the archdiocese of Prague. He opposed King Wenceslaus IV’s attempts to control the Church, and by a long tradition the king also demanded that he reveal the confession of the queen.

The king had him tortured and thrown from the Charles Bridge into the Vltava River. His statue stands on that bridge today. He is the patron of confessors, bridges, and the seal of confession.
s280.intercession: St. John Nepomucene, pray for us. Protect the seal of confession, and give priests the courage to keep it faithfully. Amen.
